real_qa.q: What are the three main elements of the dependent support test under the Succession Law Reform Act?
real_qa.r: The three-part test requires applicants to establish that they qualify as a dependent under the legislation, that the deceased was providing support or had a legal obligation to provide support immediately before death, and that the deceased failed to make adequate provisions for the applicant's support after their death.
real_qa.requete: Succession Law Reform Act dependent support test

real_qa.q: Does the definition of spouse in dependent support claims include common law partners?
real_qa.r: Yes, the definition of spouse for dependent support purposes is broader than in other areas of the Succession Law Reform Act and includes common law spouses who cohabitated continuously for at least three years, or who had a child together and were in a relationship of some permanence.
real_qa.requete: common law spouse dependent support SLRA

real_qa.q: What is the limitation period for filing a dependent support claim under the Succession Law Reform Act?
real_qa.r: The limitation period is six months from the date of probate being issued, unlike the six-month extension under the Family Law Act which runs from the date of death. This means the limitation clock starts when probate is granted, not when the person dies.
real_qa.requete: dependent support claim limitation period six months probate

real_qa.q: What are Section 72 assets that can be clawed back in a dependent support claim?
real_qa.r: Section 72 assets include jointly held assets, assets in trusts, amounts payable under a life insurance policy, amounts payable under designation of beneficiary under part two of the SLRA, and any gifts made in contemplation of death.
